elements.texte:
[cheerful] Prebiotic Fiber is arriving on the site in a new flavor: lemon.

The marketing team wants to announce this new product to the customers who have already ordered Prebiotic Fiber.

To let them know, we want to get the customers’ first and last names from the customers table.

To check whether a customer has already ordered Prebiotic Fiber, we need to look in the orders table.
elements.avant: Check whether linked rows exist or not in another table.
elements.apres: The customers table contains the customers’ information, but not the products they ordered.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] The customers table contains the customers’ information, but not the products they ordered.

In the orders table, customer underscore ID says which customer placed the order

And product underscore ID which product they ordered.

Prebiotic Fiber has the ID 1.

So we find its orders with product underscore ID equals 1: here, there are four.

To keep a customer, it’s enough to find at least one order of this product in their name.

For each customer, we check whether they placed at least one order of Prebiotic Fiber.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] EXISTS checks whether a subquery returns at least one row.

If it does, the result is true; otherwise, it’s false.

For Nathan Petit, with ID 4,

The subquery finds an order of Prebiotic Fiber: order number 5.

A row is found: EXISTS is true. So Nathan is one of the customers to notify.

For Lucas Bernard, with ID 2,

No order of this product is found: EXISTS is false.

With EXISTS, we only want to know whether a row exists.

So we write select 1, without getting the order’s details.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] To follow each customer, the hard-coded ID becomes customers dot ID.

It’s the ID of the customer on the current row: the subquery is correlated.

The condition and orders dot product underscore ID equals 1

Limits the search to the Prebiotic Fiber orders placed by this customer.

Customer after customer, EXISTS gives its verdict: true or false.

EXISTS is true for Sophie, Nathan Petit, Chloé and Léa:

Indeed, these four customers have already ordered Prebiotic Fiber.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] Without the condition orders dot customer underscore ID equals customers dot ID, the query runs,

But no longer checks whether the order belongs to the customer in question.

Without the link to the customer, the subquery looks for an order of Prebiotic Fiber,

No matter who placed it.

An order of this product exists, but its customer isn’t checked.

EXISTS is therefore true for all 10 customers, even those who never ordered this product.

Inès Lefebvre and Nathan Dupont, who never ordered anything, would get the announcement.

[cheerful] The complete query shows the first and last names of the customers

Who placed at least one order of Prebiotic Fiber.

The four customers get the announcement of the new flavor.
